title: Keep the score
description: Add up the points from every round of the riddle keeper's game, count the empty rounds, and find the average.

tasks.title: Build up an answer, one turn at a time
tasks.body: A running total starts at 0 before the loop. Inside the loop, total = total + coins adds this turn's number to what is already there. When the loop ends, total holds the sum of them all.
tasks.detail: A counter works the same way, but adds 1 each time something happens, often inside an if. The start line goes above the loop, so it runs once: inside the loop it would wipe the total every turn. For an average, divide the total by how many numbers there were, after the loop.

tasks.code:
# Three chests: add up the coins, then find the average
chests = 3
total = 0
for chest in range(chests):
    coins = int(input("Coins in this chest? "))
    total = total + coins
print(total)
print(total / chests)
tasks.note: total starts at 0 and grows: 4, then 4 again, then 12. The two print lines are below the loop, not indented, so they run once, after the last chest. Dividing with / always gives a float, so the average shows as 4.0.

tasks.question: Suppose total = 0 moves inside the loop, as the first line of its block. With the same replies, what would print(total) show?
tasks.why: total goes back to 0 at the start of every turn, so each chest forgets the ones before it. Only the last chest's 8 is left when the loop ends.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: move total = 0 inside the loop, as the first line of its block, and check your prediction. Put it back above the loop. Then add a counter for empty chests: start it above the loop, add 1 inside an if, and print it at the end.

The riddle keeper's game now has rounds. Ask how many rounds were played (always at least 1), then ask for the points from each round. Print three lines: the total points, how many rounds scored 0, and the average points per round, using /. Print just the numbers.
tasks.starter: # Ask for the rounds, then the points from each round
hints: You need two things that build up as the loop runs, and both start at 0 above the loop: one for the points, and one for the rounds that scored 0.
A for loop over range() runs once per round. Ask for that round's points inside it. The three print lines go after the loop, with no indent.
A pattern with other names: start with distance = 0, and inside the loop use distance = distance + miles. Your loop also needs a counter, and an if to decide when it goes up.

error_hints.text: A reply from input() is text. Turn it into a number with int(...) before you add it up or use it in range().
Give each name a value before the loop uses it, and spell it the same way every time.
The lines that repeat start with four spaces. A line inside an if inside the loop starts with eight.
Your loop asked for more points than there were rounds. range(rounds) already runs exactly once per round.
The average divides by the number of rounds played, and that is always at least 1. Check which number comes after the /.
With one round of 10 points, the lines are 10, 0 and 10.0. A total or a counter that starts above 0 is already wrong here, and // gives 10 where / gives 10.0.
With rounds of 10, 0 and 5, the lines are 15, 1 and 5.0. If your total says 5, it goes back to 0 on every turn: its start line belongs above the loop.
With two rounds of 0, the lines are 0, 2 and 0.0. Every round that scores 0 counts, even when nothing has been scored yet.
Check a longer game: use the number of rounds in range() and in the average, and / rather than //, which throws away the part after the point.
Check a game with more than one empty round: the counter goes up every time a round scores 0.

similar_example.code:
gold = 1
for day in range(3):
    gold = gold * 2
print(gold)
similar_example.note: Another answer that builds up: the gold doubles each day, giving 8 after three days. It starts at 1, because doubling 0 would stay 0. Your challenge adds up every round and counts the empty ones instead.

other_ways.code:
rounds = int(input("Rounds? "))
total = 0
empty = 0
count = 0
while count < rounds:
    points = int(input("Points? "))
    total = total + points
    if points == 0:
        empty = empty + 1
    count = count + 1
print(total)
print(empty)
print(total / rounds)
other_ways.note: The same totals with a while loop, which needs its own count of the rounds so far. for and range() do that counting for you.

other_ways.code:
rounds = int(input("Rounds? "))
total = 0
scored = 0
for game in range(rounds):
    points = int(input("Points? "))
    total += points
    if points > 0:
        scored += 1
print(total)
print(rounds - scored)
print(total / rounds)
other_ways.note: Count the rounds that scored instead, and take them away from all the rounds. += is a short way to write total = total + points.
